scene: The war's current address: a crowded evening subway car, every face washed in the cold blue undersides of held devices — except ONE passenger mid-car who has looked UP, face turned to the window where the last daylight is running along the tunnel's mouth, lit warm and different. No screen contents visible anywhere; no face toward the lens.
must_show: a device-lit subway car with one upturned face caught in warm window light
must_not_show: readable screens, brand marks, faces to camera, caricature

scene: The originals: the premortal court reprised — the warm bright dais-side at the frame's left with the white-robed hosts gathered, and the frame's right third gone cold and dim and EMPTY, its boundary one smooth formless fade. The two speeches, staged the way episode one staged them. Camera high behind the crowd; no face back.
must_show: the split court reprise — warm gathered left, cold empty dim right, smooth formless boundary
must_not_show: any shape in the dim, faces to camera, weapons

scene: You deserve this: a night-lit luxury storefront window of watches and leather without one readable brand — and hovering in the glass, the transparent reflection of a longing face gazing in, ghost-faint over the goods, streetlight rain-sheen on the pavement. The whisper, in retail.
must_show: an anonymous luxury window with a ghost-faint longing reflection hovering over the goods
must_not_show: readable brands or prices, the person solid, faces to lens

scene: The PR campaign: a huge street-corner billboard at dusk that is simply BLACK — a clean unmarked void over the busy sidewalk, no message, no image, nothing — while the crowd streams beneath it unbothered, nobody looking up. The best trick, rendered: a presence with no face, advertising its own absence.
must_show: a clean unmarked black billboard over an unbothered streaming crowd at dusk
must_not_show: any text or logo on the board, any figure in its black, faces to lens

scene: The awful chains, house edition: a nightstand at three a.m. — a phone face-down still leaking cold light at its edges, and its charging cord coiled around itself in tight loops across the wood like a small white chain — a glass of water untouched, the sleeper's blurred shape beyond. Domestic. Quiet. Holding.
must_show: a face-down leaking phone with its cord coiled chain-like on a 3 a.m. nightstand, sleeper blurred beyond
must_not_show: readable screen, brand marks, horror styling

scene: All is well: a beautiful comfortable living room at NOON — deep sofa, feet in wool socks up on the ottoman, steam off a mug, soft lamplight — and every curtain DRAWN SHUT, the blazing midday edging the fabric in thin gold lines the room has chosen not to receive. Prosperity, with the light shut out.
must_show: a cozy noon living room with feet up and every curtain shut, daylight edging the fabric
must_not_show: squalor, screens readable, people's faces, gloom styling

scene: Carefully down: a gleaming mall escalator descending — one relaxed man riding it down, coffee in hand, jacket open, perfectly at ease, the polished chrome and warm retail light carrying him smoothly lower — seen from the floor below at the escalator's foot. Nothing sinister in frame; that is the point.
must_show: one at-ease coffee-holding man descending a gleaming escalator, seen from below
must_not_show: readable storefronts, crowds, his face to the lens, darkness

scene: Heaven's style guide: a grandmother's floured hands guide a child's small hands INTO bread dough on a wooden table — teaching by covering, not gripping, her patience visible in the lightness of the touch, morning kitchen light, flour in the air like weather. Persuasion, gentleness, love unfeigned — in one lesson.
must_show: a grandmother's light floured hands guiding a child's hands into dough, morning kitchen light
must_not_show: faces to camera, mess played for chaos, brand marks

scene: Long-suffering, live: a father KNEELS to toddler height in a hallway before his mid-tantrum child — his arms open and resting on his knees, not grabbing, not looming, his face calm and level with the small red furious one — waiting out the storm at eye level with the storm. Power, declining to be used.
must_show: a father kneeling eye-level to a tantruming toddler, arms open and ungrabbing, calm
must_not_show: anger in the father, spanking, faces to camera

scene: Check the return address: two envelopes side by side on a doormat — one printed in shouting red blocks and urgent stamps, all of it unreadable; one plain cream paper with a few lines of soft unreadable handwriting — morning light across both. Same mat. Different senders. You can tell before you open them.
must_show: a shouting red unreadable envelope beside a plain handwritten one on a doormat

scene: Mormon's sorter: at a farm table by warm lamplight, a woman's practiced hands sort a heap of apples into two baskets — the sound one going right, a bruised one going left, one apple held mid-judgment in her palm — the evening's harvest becoming two clean bins. Every voice in your day, in fruit.
must_show: hands sorting apples into two baskets by lamplight, one apple held mid-judgment
must_not_show: her face prominent, rot graphic, text

scene: The harder right, made physical: five a.m. — a runner sliding their phone into a dresser drawer and pushing it SHUT with a knuckle, running shoes already laced in the lamplight, the window behind still night-black. The vote, re-cast before sunrise. Face unseen.
must_show: a hand pushing a phone into a drawer at 5 a.m., laced running shoes waiting, face unseen

scene: The other speech, hunting: a bank of slot machines' carnival light washing over one slack motionless face — eyes reflecting the spin, hand resting on the button out of habit rather than hope, the rest of the room falling to black around the machine's embrace. No brands, no readable reels. A throne, being sat on.
must_show: slot-light washing a slack motionless face, habitual hand on the button, room falling to black

scene: The vote as a doorbell: a casserole dish balanced on one arm while the other hand presses a neighbor's doorbell — evening porch light warming the foil and the knuckle, a welcome mat below, the door a breath from opening. Service: the oldest ballot there is.
must_show: a casserole balanced on one arm while a finger presses a porch doorbell at evening

scene: In the cast: the hallway mirror from episode two — but now the person stands square to it and the reflection is CLEAR: an ordinary face meeting its own eyes calmly, chin level, morning light even across the glass. The veil-washed stranger of episode two, replaced by somebody who knows their name.
must_show: a person square to the hallway mirror with a CLEAR calm reflection meeting their own eyes
must_not_show: the reflection looking at the camera instead, bathroom clutter, brand marks

scene: Heaven's way, working: in a warm living room, two men stand behind a seated young woman with their hands resting gently together on her head in blessing — her eyes closed, her mother's hand in hers, a grandfather watching with wet eyes from the sofa arm — priesthood operating exactly per the style guide. Reverent, plain, quiet.
must_show: two men's gentle hands together on a seated woman's head in blessing, family close, eyes closed

scene: The daily truce: a city skyline at first light — the night's window-lights going out block by block as the sunrise takes over the job, the sky clean, the streets still. The war pauses for no one; the light still wins the morning, every morning. No people.
must_show: city window-lights going out block by block as sunrise takes over, clean sky
